# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

```plantuml
@startuml

title conference Model

class Author {
    papers : List<Paper>
    calculateAcceptanceRate() : double
    countSubmittedPapers() : int
    submitPaper(paper : Paper) : void
}
class CoChair {
    makeFinalDecision(paper : Paper, decision : Grade) : int
}
class Paper {
    decision : Grade
    title : String
    type : PaperType
    reviews : List<ReviewAssignment>
    isAllReviewsConsistent() : boolean
}
class ReviewAssignment {
    feedback : String
    grade : Grade
    paper : Paper
}
class Reviewer {
    assignments : List<ReviewAssignment>
    calculateSubmittedReviewAverageScore() : double
    calculateUnsubmittedReviews() : int
}
class User {
    name : String
    roles : List<UserRole>
}
abstract class UserRole {
    id : String
}
enum Grade {
    UNDECIDED
    ACCEPT
    REJECT
}
enum PaperType {
    RESEARCH
    EXPERIENCE
}

Author --|> UserRole
Author --> "*" Paper : papers
CoChair --|> UserRole
Paper --> "*" ReviewAssignment : reviews  'opposite: paper
ReviewAssignment --> Paper : paper  'opposite: reviews
Reviewer --|> UserRole
Reviewer --> "*" ReviewAssignment : assignments
User *-- "*" UserRole : roles
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

# Operation Specifications
Paper::isAllReviewsConsistent
Summary:
  Checks whether all reviews for this paper are consistent, meaning
  every submitted review is either exclusively ACCEPT or exclusively
  REJECT. Returns false when there are no reviews, fewer than 3
  reviews, or any UNDECIDED review is present.
Algorithm:
  1. If reviews == null or reviews.size() < 3, return false.
  2. Let allAccept = true, allReject = true.
  3. For each ReviewAssignment r in reviews:
       if r.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return false.
       if r.grade != Grade.ACCEPT, allAccept = false.
       if r.grade != Grade.REJECT, allReject = false.
  4. Return (allAccept || allReject).
Related Features:
  - reviews : List<ReviewAssignment>  (iterated for size and contents)
  - ReviewAssignment.grade : Grade   (read for consistency evaluation)
  - Grade enum values: UNDECIDED, ACCEPT, REJECT
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input:
  None (operates on the receiver Paper instance).
Output:
  boolean — true  if at least 3 reviews exist and they are all
                 either ACCEPT or all REJECT (no UNDECIDED);
            false otherwise (including the no-reviews case).
Pre-condition:
  - The Paper instance is properly initialized with its reviews list
    (possibly empty).
Post-condition:
  - The state of the Paper and its reviews is unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
CoChair::makeFinalDecision
Summary:
  Attempts to set the final decision (ACCEPT or REJECT) for a paper.
  The decision is applied only when the paper satisfies the strict
  review-consistency rules; otherwise, the paper's decision is left
  unchanged and -1 is returned.
Algorithm:
  1. If paper is null or decision is null, return -1.
  2. Validate the decision value:
       if decision is not Grade.ACCEPT and not Grade.REJECT
       (e.g., UNDECIDED), return -1.
  3. If paper.reviews.size() < 3, return -1.
  4. For each review r in paper.reviews:
       if r.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return -1.
  5. Determine consistency:
       - allAccept = true if every review.grade == ACCEPT, else false.
       - allReject = true if every review.grade == REJECT, else false.
       If not (allAccept || allReject), return -1.
  6. Set paper.decision = decision.
  7. Return 1.

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. 4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.

# Operation Specifications
CoChair::makeFinalDecision
Summary:
  Attempts to set the final decision (ACCEPT or REJECT) for a paper.
  The decision is applied only when the paper satisfies the strict
  review-consistency rules; otherwise, the paper's decision is left
  unchanged and -1 is returned.
Algorithm:
  1. If paper is null or decision is null, return -1.
  2. Validate the decision value:
       if decision is not Grade.ACCEPT and not Grade.REJECT
       (e.g., UNDECIDED), return -1.
  3. If paper.reviews.size() < 3, return -1.
  4. For each review r in paper.reviews:
       if r.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return -1.
  5. Determine consistency:
       - allAccept = true if every review.grade == ACCEPT, else false.
       - allReject = true if every review.grade == REJECT, else false.
       If not (allAccept || allReject), return -1.
  6. Set paper.decision = decision.
  7. Return 1.
Related Features:
  - Paper.decision : Grade  (written when the decision is finalized)
  - Paper.reviews : List<ReviewAssignment>  (inspected for size and grades)
  - ReviewAssignment.grade : Grade  (read for consistency check)
  - Grade enum values: UNDECIDED, ACCEPT, REJECT
Related Classes: Paper, ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input:
  paper : Paper    — the paper whose final decision is being made.
                     Must not be null and must have at least 3 reviews.
  decision : Grade — the proposed final decision.
                     Must be either Grade.ACCEPT or Grade.REJECT.
Output:
  int — 1  when the final decision is successfully applied;
        -1 when any of the validation/consistency checks fail
           (paper unchanged).
Pre-condition:
  - The CoChair is authenticated/authorized to make decisions.
  - The paper is properly initialized with its reviews list populated.
  - The decision argument is a valid Grade value.
Post-condition:
  - On success (return 1): paper.decision equals the supplied decision.
  - On failure (return -1): paper.decision is unchanged.
  - The papers list of any author is unaffected.

# Operation Specifications
Reviewer::calculateSubmittedReviewAverageScore
Summary:
  Converts this reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical
  average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted
  reviews (excluding UNDECIDED). ACCEPT is treated as 1 and REJECT
  as 0. Returns 0.00 when there are no submitted reviews.
Algorithm:
  1. Let sum = 0, count = 0.
  2. For each ReviewAssignment a in assignments:
       if a.grade == Grade.ACCEPT then sum += 1, count++.
       else if a.grade == Grade.REJECT then sum += 0, count++.
       (UNDECIDED reviews are skipped.)
  3. If count == 0, return 0.00.
  4. Return (double) sum / count.
Related Features:
  - assignments : List<ReviewAssignment>  (iterated to gather grades)
  - ReviewAssignment.grade : Grade        (read and converted to numeric)
  - Grade enum values: ACCEPT, REJECT, UNDECIDED
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input:
  None (operates on the receiver Reviewer instance).
Output:
  double — the average score in the range [0.0, 1.0].
  Returns 0.00 when no submitted reviews exist.
  Expected precision: within 0.001 of the true average.
Pre-condition:
  - The Reviewer instance is properly initialized.
  - Each ReviewAssignment has a valid Grade value.
Post-condition:
  - The state of the Reviewer and its assignments is unchanged.
  - The returned value is finite and within [0.0, 1.0].

Reviewer::calculateUnsubmittedReviews
Summary:
  Calculates the number of unsubmitted reviews assigned to this
  reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted when its grade is
  UNDECIDED. Returns 0 when the reviewer has no assignments or all
  reviews are submitted.
Algorithm:
  1. If assignments is null or empty, return 0.
  2. Let count = 0.
  3. For each ReviewAssignment a in assignments:
       if a.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED then count++.
  4. Return count.
Related Features:
  - assignments : List<ReviewAssignment>  (iterated to count grades)
  - ReviewAssignment.grade : Grade        (read to check UNDECIDED)
  - Grade enum value: UNDECIDED
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input:
  None (operates on the receiver Reviewer instance).
Output:
  int — the number of unsubmitted reviews (>= 0).
        Returns 0 if the reviewer has no assignments or all reviews
        are submitted.
Pre-condition:
  - The Reviewer instance is properly initialized.
  - Each ReviewAssignment has a valid Grade value.
Post-condition:
  - The state of the Reviewer and its assignments is unchanged.

The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

  Returns the total number of papers submitted by this author.

Post-condition:
  - The state of the Author is unchanged.

Author::submitPaper
Summary:
  Adds a paper to this author's list of submitted papers.
  Establishes the authorship relationship between the author and the paper.
Algorithm:
  1. If paper is null, throw IllegalArgumentException (input validation).
  2. Append paper to this.papers.
Related Features:
  - papers : List<Paper>  (mutated by adding the new paper)
Related Classes: Paper
Input:
  paper : Paper — the paper being submitted; must not be null.
          It is expected to have its title and type set, and its
          reviews list initialized (possibly empty).
Output:
  void — no return value.
Pre-condition:
  - The paper is not null.
  - The paper has not already been submitted by this author
    (caller's responsibility; this method does not check duplicates).
Post-condition:
  - The paper is included in this.papers.
  - The size of papers is increased by 1.

Author::calculateAcceptanceRate
Summary:
  Computes the acceptance rate of papers submitted by this author.
  The rate is the ratio of accepted papers to total papers submitted.
  Returns 0.00 when the author has no papers.
Algorithm:
  1. Let total = papers.size().
  2. If total == 0, return 0.00.
  3. Let accepted = 0.
  4. For each paper p in papers:
       if p.decision == Grade.ACCEPT then accepted++.
  5. Return (double) accepted / total.
Related Features:
  - papers : List<Paper>  (iterated to evaluate each paper's decision)
  - Paper.decision : Grade (read to check whether the paper was accepted)
  - Grade enum values: ACCEPT (compared against)
Related Classes: Paper, Grade
Input:
  None (operates on the receiver Author instance).
Output:
  double — the acceptance rate in the range [0.0, 1.0].
  Returns 0.00 when the author has no papers.
  Expected precision: within 0.001 of the true rate.
Pre-condition:
  - The Author instance must be properly initialized.
  - Each Paper in papers has a defined decision (Grade value).
Post-condition:
  - The state of the Author and its papers is unchanged.
  - The returned double is a finite value in [0.0, 1.0].

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

   * Post-condition:

    if (assignmentsList == null || assignmentsList.isEmpty())
    {
      return 0;
    }
    int count = 0;
    for (ReviewAssignment a : assignmentsList)

        count++;
      }
    }

  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Converts this reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical
   *   average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted
   *   reviews (excluding UNDECIDED). ACCEPT is treated as 1 and REJECT
   *   as 0. Returns 0.00 when there are no submitted reviews.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Let sum = 0, count = 0.
   *   2. For each ReviewAssignment a in assignments:
   *        if a.grade == Grade.ACCEPT then sum += 1, count++.
   *        else if a.grade == Grade.REJECT then sum += 0, count++.
   *        (UNDECIDED reviews are skipped.)
   *   3. If count == 0, return 0.00.
   *   4. Return (double) sum / count.
   * Related Features:
   *   - assignments : List<ReviewAssignment>  (iterated to gather grades)
   *   - ReviewAssignment.grade : Grade        (read and converted to numeric)
   *   - Grade enum values: ACCEPT, REJECT, UNDECIDED
   * Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
   * Input:
   *   None (operates on the receiver Reviewer instance).
   * Output:
   *   double — the average score in the range [0.0, 1.0].
   *   Returns 0.00 when no submitted reviews exist.
   *   Expected precision: within 0.001 of the true average.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - The Reviewer instance is properly initialized.
   *   - Each ReviewAssignment has a valid Grade value.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The state of the Reviewer and its assignments is unchanged.
   *   - The returned value is finite and within [0.0, 1.0].
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public double calculateSubmittedReviewAverageScore()
  {
    EList<ReviewAssignment> assignmentsList = getAssignments();
    int sum = 0;
    int count = 0;
    if (assignmentsList != null)
    {
      for (ReviewAssignment a : assignmentsList)
      {
        Grade grade = a.getGrade();
        if (grade == Grade.ACCEPT)
        {
          sum += 1;
          count++;
        }
        else if (grade == Grade.REJECT)
        {
          sum += 0;
          count++;
        }
      }
    }
    if (count == 0)
    {
      return 0.00;
    }
    return (double) sum / count;
  }

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

title conference Model

}

}

    feedback : String
    grade : Grade
    paper : Paper
}

    calculateSubmittedReviewAverageScore() : double
    calculateUnsubmittedReviews() : int
}

    name : String
    roles : List<UserRole>
}
abstract class UserRole {
    id : String
}
enum Grade {
    UNDECIDED
    ACCEPT
    REJECT
}
enum PaperType {
    RESEARCH
    EXPERIENCE
}

Author --|> UserRole
Author --> "*" Paper : papers
CoChair --|> UserRole
Paper --> "*" ReviewAssignment : reviews  'opposite: paper
ReviewAssignment --> Paper : paper  'opposite: reviews
Reviewer --|> UserRole

User *-- "*" UserRole : roles
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

Related Features: papers (List<Paper>)

        with an error margin of 0.001. Returns 0.00 if the author

               or already initialized; each paper in this.papers has
               a decision of one of the Grade enum values.
Post-condition: The author's papers list is unchanged; a non-negative
                double value representing the acceptance rate is returned.

# Operation Specifications
CoChair::makeFinalDecision
Summary: Attempts to set the final decision for a paper. The decision is
         applied only when the paper has at least three reviews, none of
         which is UNDECIDED, and all reviews are consistent (either all
         ACCEPT or all REJECT). Returns 1 on success and -1 on failure.
Algorithm:
  1. If paper.reviews.size() < 3, return -1.
  2. For each review in paper.reviews:
       if review.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return -1.
  3. If !paper.isAllReviewsConsistent(), return -1.
  4. Set paper.decision = decision.
  5. Return 1.
Related Features: decision (Grade)
Related Classes: Paper, ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input: paper : Paper - the paper whose final decision is being set;
                  must not be null.
       decision : Grade - the proposed final decision (ACCEPT or REJECT);
                  must not be UNDECIDED.
Output: int - 1 if the decision was successfully set on the paper;
             -1 if any of the three conditions (>=3 reviews, no UNDECIDED
             reviews, consistent reviews) is not met, in which case the
             paper's decision remains unchanged.
Pre-condition: The co-chair instance exists; the paper parameter is a valid,
               non-null Paper object; the decision parameter is a valid
               Grade value (ACCEPT or REJECT).
Post-condition: On success (return 1), paper.decision is set to the given
                decision value. On failure (return -1), paper.decision
                remains unchanged.

For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

# Operation Specifications
CoChair::makeFinalDecision
Summary: Attempts to set the final decision for a paper. The decision is
         applied only when the paper has at least three reviews, none of
         which is UNDECIDED, and all reviews are consistent (either all
         ACCEPT or all REJECT). Returns 1 on success and -1 on failure.
Algorithm:
  1. If paper.reviews.size() < 3, return -1.
  2. For each review in paper.reviews:
       if review.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return -1.
  3. If !paper.isAllReviewsConsistent(), return -1.
  4. Set paper.decision = decision.
  5. Return 1.
Related Features: decision (Grade)
Related Classes: Paper, ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input: paper : Paper - the paper whose final decision is being set;
                  must not be null.
       decision : Grade - the proposed final decision (ACCEPT or REJECT);
                  must not be UNDECIDED.
Output: int - 1 if the decision was successfully set on the paper;
             -1 if any of the three conditions (>=3 reviews, no UNDECIDED
             reviews, consistent reviews) is not met, in which case the
             paper's decision remains unchanged.
Pre-condition: The co-chair instance exists; the paper parameter is a valid,
               non-null Paper object; the decision parameter is a valid
               Grade value (ACCEPT or REJECT).
Post-condition: On success (return 1), paper.decision is set to the given
                decision value. On failure (return -1), paper.decision
                remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.

# Operation Specifications
Reviewer::calculateSubmittedReviewAverageScore
Summary: Converts this reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical
         average score between 0.0 and 1.0. Only submitted reviews (those
         with grade ACCEPT or REJECT) are considered; ACCEPT is treated
         as 1 and REJECT as 0.
Algorithm:
  1. submitted = 0; sum = 0.
  2. For each assignment in this.assignments:
       if assignment.grade == Grade.ACCEPT then sum += 1; submitted++.
       else if assignment.grade == Grade.REJECT then sum += 0; submitted++.
       (UNDECIDED reviews are skipped.)
  3. If submitted == 0, return 0.00.
  4. Return sum / submitted (as double).
Related Features: assignments (List<ReviewAssignment>)
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input: None
Output: double - the average score in the range [0.00, 1.00],
        with an error margin of 0.001. Returns 0.00 if there are no
        submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments).
Pre-condition: The reviewer instance exists; this.assignments is initialized
               (possibly empty); each assignment's grade is a valid Grade
               enum value.
Post-condition: The reviewer's assignments list is unchanged; a double
                value representing the average score is returned.

Reviewer::calculateUnsubmittedReviews
Summary: Calculates the number of unsubmitted reviews assigned to this
         reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is
         UNDECIDED.
Algorithm:
  1. count = 0.
  2. For each assignment in this.assignments:
       if assignment.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED then count++.
  3. Return count.
Related Features: assignments (List<ReviewAssignment>)
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input: None
Output: int - the number of unsubmitted reviews (>= 0). Returns 0 if
             all reviews are submitted or if the reviewer has no
             assignments.
Pre-condition: The reviewer instance exists; this.assignments is initialized
               (possibly empty); each assignment's grade is a valid Grade
               enum value.
Post-condition: The reviewer's assignments list is unchanged; the count
                of UNDECIDED reviews is returned as an integer.

# Operation Specifications
Paper::isAllReviewsConsistent
Summary: Checks whether all reviews for this paper are exclusively ACCEPT
         or exclusively REJECT. Returns false if there are no reviews or
         if any review is UNDECIDED.
Algorithm:
  1. If this.reviews is empty, return false.
  2. Let first = this.reviews.get(0).grade.
  3. If first == Grade.UNDECIDED, return false.
  4. For each review in this.reviews (from index 1 onward):
       if review.grade != first, return false.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: reviews (List<ReviewAssignment>)
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if all reviews have the same non-UNDECIDED grade
                  (all ACCEPT or all REJECT); false otherwise (including
                  when the paper has no reviews or any review is UNDECIDED).
Pre-condition: The paper instance exists; this.reviews is initialized
               (possibly empty); each review's grade is a valid Grade
               enum value.
Post-condition: The paper's reviews list is unchanged; a boolean result
                is returned.

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

# Operation Specifications
Paper::isAllReviewsConsistent
Summary: Checks whether all reviews for this paper are exclusively ACCEPT
         or exclusively REJECT. Returns false if there are no reviews or
         if any review is UNDECIDED.
Algorithm:
  1. If this.reviews is empty, return false.
  2. Let first = this.reviews.get(0).grade.
  3. If first == Grade.UNDECIDED, return false.
  4. For each review in this.reviews (from index 1 onward):
       if review.grade != first, return false.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: reviews (List<ReviewAssignment>)
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if all reviews have the same non-UNDECIDED grade
                  (all ACCEPT or all REJECT); false otherwise (including
                  when the paper has no reviews or any review is UNDECIDED).
Pre-condition: The paper instance exists; this.reviews is initialized
               (possibly empty); each review's grade is a valid Grade
               enum value.
Post-condition: The paper's reviews list is unchanged; a boolean result
                is returned.

public double calculateSubmittedReviewAverageScore()
{
  int submitted = 0;
  int sum = 0;
  for (ReviewAssignment assignment : getAssignments())
  {
    if (assignment.getGrade() == Grade.ACCEPT)
    {
      sum += 1;
      submitted++;
    }
    else if (assignment.getGrade() == Grade.REJECT)
    {
      sum += 0;
      submitted++;
    }
  }
  if (submitted == 0)
  {
    return 0.00;
  }
  return (double) sum / submitted;
}

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

title conference Model

class Author {
    papers : List<Paper>
    calculateAcceptanceRate() : double

    submitPaper(paper : Paper) : void

    makeFinalDecision(paper : Paper, decision : Grade) : int
}
class Paper {
    decision : Grade
    title : String
    type : PaperType
    reviews : List<ReviewAssignment>
    isAllReviewsConsistent() : boolean
}
class ReviewAssignment {
    feedback : String
    grade : Grade
    paper : Paper
}
class Reviewer {
    assignments : List<ReviewAssignment>
    calculateSubmittedReviewAverageScore() : double
    calculateUnsubmittedReviews() : int
}
class User {
    name : String
    roles : List<UserRole>
}
abstract class UserRole {
    id : String
}
enum Grade {
    UNDECIDED
    ACCEPT
    REJECT
}
enum PaperType {
    RESEARCH
    EXPERIENCE
}

Author --|> UserRole
Author --> "*" Paper : papers
CoChair --|> UserRole
Paper --> "*" ReviewAssignment : reviews  'opposite: paper
ReviewAssignment --> Paper : paper  'opposite: reviews
Reviewer --|> UserRole
Reviewer --> "*" ReviewAssignment : assignments
User *-- "*" UserRole : roles
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

# Operation Specifications
Author::submitPaper
Summary: Adds a given paper to this author's list of submitted papers, registering authorship of the paper.
Algorithm:
  1. If paper is null, throw IllegalArgumentException (or return without action).
  2. Add paper to this.papers.
  3. (Optionally) Set the paper's author reference if such a back-pointer exists.
Related Features: papers (List<Paper>)
Related Classes: Paper
Input: paper : Paper - the paper to be submitted; must be a non-null Paper instance with a valid title and type.
Output: void
Pre-condition: The paper parameter is a non-null Paper instance that has been properly constructed (with a title and PaperType). The author is authenticated and authorized to submit papers.
Post-condition: The given paper is appended to this.papers. The author's submitted paper count increases by one.

Author::calculateAcceptanceRate
Summary: Computes the acceptance rate of all papers submitted by this author, defined as the ratio of accepted papers to total submitted papers. Returns 0.00 when the author has no papers.
Algorithm:
  1. Let total = this.papers.size().
  2. If total == 0, return 0.00.
  3. Let accepted = 0.
  4. For each paper p in this.papers:
       If p.decision == Grade.ACCEPT, increment accepted.
  5. Return accepted / total as a double.
Related Features: papers (List<Paper>)
Related Classes: Paper, Grade
Input: None
Output: double - the acceptance rate in the range [0.00, 1.00], with precision within 0.001. Returns 0.00 when there are no papers.
Pre-condition: The Author instance has been properly initialized. Each Paper in the papers list has a valid decision value (Grade.ACCEPT, Grade.REJECT, or possibly another value, though only ACCEPT counts as accepted).
Post-condition: The state of the Author and its papers is unchanged. The returned value reflects the current acceptance rate.

Author::countSubmittedPapers
Summary: Returns the total number of papers that have been submitted by this author.
Algorithm:
  1. Return this.papers.size().
Related Features: papers (List<Paper>)
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: int - a non-negative integer representing the total number of papers submitted by this author.
Pre-condition: The Author instance has been properly initialized with a papers list (possibly empty).
Post-condition: The state of the Author is unchanged. The returned value equals the number of papers in the papers list.

# Operation Specifications
Paper::isAllReviewsConsistent
Summary: Determines whether all submitted reviews for this paper are exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject (i.e., unanimous). Returns false if there are no reviews, if any review is UNDECIDED, or if reviews are mixed.
Algorithm:
  1. If this.reviews == null or this.reviews.isEmpty(), return false.
  2. Let firstGrade = this.reviews.get(0).grade.
  3. If firstGrade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return false.
  4. For each ReviewAssignment ra in this.reviews (from index 1 onward):
       If ra.grade != firstGrade, return false.
       If ra.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return false.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: reviews (List<ReviewAssignment>)
Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if all reviews share the same grade and that grade is either ACCEPT or REJECT (and there is at least one review); false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Paper instance has been properly initialized with a reviews list (possibly empty).
Post-condition: The state of the Paper is unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
CoChair::makeFinalDecision
Summary: Sets the final decision for a given paper only when all review consistency conditions are satisfied; otherwise leaves the decision unchanged. Returns an integer status code indicating success (1) or failure (-1).
Algorithm:
  1. If paper is null, return -1.
  2. If paper.reviews == null or paper.reviews.size() < 3, return -1.
  3. If any review in paper.reviews has grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return -1.
  4. If !paper.isAllReviewsConsistent(), return -1.
  5. Otherwise, set paper.decision = decision (the supplied Grade) and return 1.
Related Features: (operates on Paper attributes via parameter)
Related Classes: Paper, ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input:
  - paper : Paper - the paper for which the final decision is to be made; must be non-null and have at least three reviews.
  - decision : Grade - the final decision to assign (Grade.ACCEPT or Grade.REJECT).

# Requirement
```text
To help the program chair, we are planning to develop a computer-assisted review system. The system will be available to users who can be authors, reviewers, and co-chairs. Each user has a name. Each user role (author, reviewer, or co-chair) has an id to identify the role. Papers are known by the title and whether they are research papers or experience report papers. The paper is reviewed by at least three reviewers. On the other side, the authors can submit as many papers as they want. When a reviewer logs in, she can consult the list of papers that have been assigned to her for review, and submit reviews for each of those papers. Each review has feedback as well as grade. Before submission the grade is UNDECIDED, and after submission it becomes ACCEPT or REJECT. A final decision is made by the co-chair for each paper.
Functional Requirement:
1.Calculate the number of unsubmitted reviews for a given reviewer. A review is considered unsubmitted if its grade is UNDECIDED. Return 0 if all reviews are submitted by the reviewer or if the reviewer has no assignments.

2.Before the chair makes the final decision, check whether all reviews for a paper (from at least three reviewers) are either exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject. Return a boolean value. If a paper has no reviews, or if any review is UNDECIDED, the reviews are not considered consistent (return false). The CoChair's makeFinalDecision method should return 1 and set the paper's decision only when all three conditions are met: at least 3 reviews, no UNDECIDED reviews, and all reviews are consistent; otherwise return -1 and leave the paper's decision unchanged.

3.Count the total number of papers submitted by an author.

4.Calculate the acceptance rate of papers for an author. Example: If an author submitted 10 papers with 6 accepted, return 0.60. If the author has no papers, return 0.00.

5.Convert a reviewer's submitted review grades into a numerical average score between 0.0 and 1.0, considering only submitted reviews (excluding UNDECIDED) and treating ACCEPT as 1 and REJECT as 0. For example, for 3 ACCEPT and 1 REJECT, the average score is (3×1 + 1×0)/4 = 0.75. The result should be within an error margin of 0.001. If there are no submitted reviews (all UNDECIDED or no assignments), return 0.00.


```

# Operation Specifications
CoChair::makeFinalDecision
Summary: Sets the final decision for a given paper only when all review consistency conditions are satisfied; otherwise leaves the decision unchanged. Returns an integer status code indicating success (1) or failure (-1).
Algorithm:
  1. If paper is null, return -1.
  2. If paper.reviews == null or paper.reviews.size() < 3, return -1.
  3. If any review in paper.reviews has grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return -1.
  4. If !paper.isAllReviewsConsistent(), return -1.
  5. Otherwise, set paper.decision = decision (the supplied Grade) and return 1.
Related Features: (operates on Paper attributes via parameter)
Related Classes: Paper, ReviewAssignment, Grade
Input:
  - paper : Paper - the paper for which the final decision is to be made; must be non-null and have at least three reviews.
  - decision : Grade - the final decision to assign (Grade.ACCEPT or Grade.REJECT).
Output: int - returns 1 if the decision was successfully applied; returns -1 if any condition failed (paper is null, fewer than 3 reviews, any UNDECIDED review, or reviews are not consistent).
Pre-condition: The CoChair is authenticated. The paper has at least three reviews assigned. The decision parameter is a valid Grade value.
Post-condition: When 1 is returned, paper.decision is updated to the supplied decision. When -1 is returned, paper.decision remains unchanged.

1. Compute context information
  1.1 Navigate the Ecore model to find related classes
  1.2 Also consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.3 Locate these files in your project.
  1.4 Generate the class summarization.
2. A method is unimplemented if its body contains `// TODO: Please complete this Java method based on the docstring`.
3. For every unimplemented method, 
  3.1 You must read the docstring of this method. The fragment between `<!-- begin-model-doc -->` and `<!-- end-model-doc -->` contains the method specification;
  3.2 Generate your code strictly according to the algorithm; Be aware of the EMF code style and APIs;
  3.3 You should not change the method signature;
  3.4 After generation, replace the current body with the one you generate;
  3.5 Keep and update the docstring by changing `@generated` to `@generated NOT`.
4. Check the import list. Add missing imports if needed.
5. Do not change other part.
6. Be aware of the method signatures, particularly, the input and output types, provided in the **Context**.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Determines whether all reviews for this paper are exclusively Accept or exclusively Reject (i.e., unanimous), and that there are at least three reviews. Returns false if there are fewer than three reviews, if any review is UNDECIDED, or if the reviews are mixed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If this.reviews == null or this.reviews.size() < 3, return false.
   *   2. Let firstGrade = this.reviews.get(0).grade.
   *   3. If firstGrade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return false.
   *   4. For each ReviewAssignment ra in this.reviews (from index 1 onward):
   *        If ra.grade == Grade.UNDECIDED, return false.
   *        If ra.grade != firstGrade, return false.
   *   5. Return true.
   * Related Features: reviews (List<ReviewAssignment>)
   * Related Classes: ReviewAssignment, Grade
   * Input: None
   * Output: boolean - true if there are at least three reviews, none of which are UNDECIDED, and all reviews share the same grade (ACCEPT or REJECT); false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: The Paper instance has been properly initialized with a reviews list (possibly empty).
   * Post-condition: The state of the Paper is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model kind="operation"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isAllReviewsConsistent()
  {
    EList<ReviewAssignment> reviewList = getReviews();
    if (reviewList == null || reviewList.size() < 3)
    {
      return false;
    }
    Grade firstGrade = reviewList.get(0).getGrade();
    if (firstGrade == Grade.UNDECIDED)
    {
      return false;
    }
    for (int i = 1; i < reviewList.size(); i++)
    {
      ReviewAssignment ra = reviewList.get(i);
      Grade currentGrade = ra.getGrade();
      if (currentGrade == Grade.UNDECIDED || currentGrade != firstGrade)
      {
        return false;
      }
    }
    return true;
  }
